He played [[college basketball]] for the UMKC Kangaroos (now known as the [[Kansas City Roos men's basketball|Kansas City Roos]]) and the [[Miami Hurricanes men's basketball|Miami Hurricanes]].{{cite news |author1=Tim Reynolds |title=For some, 2 teams now means 2 chances |url=https://www.newspapers.com/clip/98167173/for-some-2-teams-now-means-2-chances/ |access-date=22 March 2022 |work=[[The Salinas Californian|The Californian]] |agency=[[Associated Press]] |date=7 July 2017 |page=A14|via =[[Newspapers.com]]}} {{Open access}}{{cite news |author1=Michelle Kaufman |title=McKinney Jones expands the family business |url=https://www.newspapers.com/clip/98167525/mckinney-jones-expands-the-family-busine/ |access-date=22 March 2022 |work=[[The Miami Herald]] |date=21 January 2012 |page=3D|via =[[Newspapers.com]]}} {{Open access}}{{cite news |author1=Michael Casagrande |title=Jones can do it all |url=https://www.newspapers.com/clip/98167698/jones-can-do-it-all/ |access-date=22 March 2022 |work=[[South Florida Sun Sentinel]] |date=25 March 2013 |pages=1C, 7C|via =[[Newspapers.com]]}} {{Open access}} ==College career== McKinney-Jones played two seasons at UMKC, averaging 10.9 points and 3.8 rebounds in 28.5 minutes per game as a sophomore. In his sophomore year, his high flying dunk against Centenary was selected as the ESPN SportsCenter number one play of the day. He transferred to Miami and sat out the 2010–11 season as a redshirt. As a junior at Miami, he averaged 7.0 points, 3.5 rebounds, 1.4 assists and 0.7 steals in 24.1 minutes per game. In his senior year, McKinney-Jones posted averages of 9.2 points and 3.4 rebounds in 30.3 minutes per game. In the ACC tournament versus [[North Carolina Tar Heels men's basketball|North Carolina]], he broke the school record for most three-pointers in a tournament game with six.{{cite web|title=Trey McKinney-Jones Profile|url=http://www.hurricanesports.com/ViewArticle.dbml?ATCLID=205555838|website=[[Miami Hurricanes]]|accessdate=September 28, 2015}} ==Professional career== ===Fort Wayne Mad Ants (2013–2014)=== After going undrafted in the [[2013 NBA draft]], McKinney-Jones signed with the [[Milwaukee Bucks]] for training camp on September 30, 2013.[http://www.insidehoops.com/blog/?p=14372 Bucks add Junior Cadougan, Olek Czyz, Stephen Graham, Trey McKinney Jones to training camp] He was later waived by the Bucks on October 26 after appearing in two preseason games.[http://www.insidehoops.com/blog/?p=14654 Milwaukee Bucks waive Trey McKinney Jones, Olek Czyz and Stephen Graham] The following month, he was acquired by the [[Fort Wayne Mad Ants]] of the [[NBA Development League]]. As a rookie playing for the Mad Ants in 2013–14, McKinney-Jones averaged 14.8 points, 4.5 rebounds, 2.1 assists and 1.1 steals in 53 games,[https://www.basketball-reference.com/dleague/players/j/jonestr01d.html Trey McKinney Jones D-League Stats] while helping the team win their maiden championship.[http://www.indystar.com/story/sports/basketball/2014/04/27/fort-wayne-mad-ants-win-nba-d-league-title/8274813/ Fort Wayne Mad Ants win NBA D-League title] ===Gravelines (2014)=== In July 2014, McKinney-Jones joined the [[Miami Heat]] for the Orlando Summer League and the [[San Antonio Spurs]] for the Las Vegas Summer League.[http://www.journalgazette.net/blog/mad-antics/McKinney-Jones-coming-back-to-Ants-5129755 McKinney-Jones coming back to Ants] On August 16, 2014, he signed with [[BCM Gravelines]] of France for the 2014–15 season.[http://www.sportando.com/en/europe/france/131707/trey-mckinney-jones-signs-with-gravelines-dunkerque.html Trey McKinney-Jones signs with Gravelines-Dunkerque] However, in late December, he parted ways with the Gravelines after appearing in 14 games.[http://www.sportando.com/en/europe/france/146271/trey-mckinney-jones-is-leaving-gravelines-dunkerque.html Trey McKinney-Jones is leaving Gravelines-Dunkerque] ===Return to the Mad Ants (2015)=== On February 20, 2015, he was reacquired by the Fort Wayne Mad Ants.[http://fortwayne.dleague.nba.com/news/mad-ants-reacquire-mckinney-jones/ Mad Ants Reacquire McKinney-Jones] He played out the season with the Mad Ants, and in 22 games, he averaged 11.4 points, 4.5 rebounds and 2.0 assists per game. ===Maccabi Kiryat Gat (2015)=== In July 2015, McKinney-Jones joined the [[Atlanta Hawks]] for the [[2015 NBA Summer League]]. The following month, he signed with [[Maccabi Kiryat Gat B.C.|Maccabi Kiryat Gat]] of the [[Israeli Basketball Premier League]].[http://www.sportando.com/en/europe/israel/173968/maccabi-kiryat-gat-nearing-to-an-agreement-with-trey-mckinney-jones.html Maccabi Kiryat Gat nearing to an agreement with Trey McKinney-Jones] ===Körmend (2016)=== In January 2016, McKinney-Jones joined Hungarian club [[BC Körmend|Egis Körmend]]. He was a guard on the 2015–2016 team which made it to the semifinals, falling 87–76 to [[Team 23]]. McKinney-Jones won the 2016 Hungarian Cup during his tenure with Körmend. ===Third stint with the Mad Ants (2016–2018)=== On October 31, 2016, McKinney-Jones was reacquired by the [[Fort Wayne Mad Ants]] of the [[NBA Development League]].{{cite web|first=Vinessa|last=Needham|url=http://fortwayne.dleague.nba.com/news/mad-ants-finalize-training-camp-roster-following-2016-draft/|title=Mad Ants Finalize Training Camp Roster Following 2016 Draft|work=NBA.com|date=October 31, 2016|accessdate=November 12, 2016}} On September 7, 2017, McKinney-Jones signed with the [[Indiana Pacers]] of the NBA, on a training camp deal.{{cite web|title=Pacers Sign DeQuan Jones and Trey McKinney-Jones|url=http://www.nba.com/pacers/news/pacers-sign-dequan-jones-and-trey-mckinney-jones|date=September 7,
